transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
My head’s been feeling foggy lately. I’m making little mistakes in my client notes and forgetting what I was about to do, and that’s not usually like me.
Aside from the fogginess, how has your overall mood been lately?
Lately I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. I can get through my shift and talk to people, but inside I just feel sad and kind of flat.
About how long have you been feeling this way?
It’s been about a month now—the low feeling, guilt, and that fogginess.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you normally enjoy doing?
I’m not really sure. I still do the things I normally do, I guess—I just feel kind of flat while I’m doing them.
Did any major stressful events or significant life changes happen around the time these symptoms started?
Yeah… my uncle died about two weeks ago. That’s really when this whole shift started.
How has your sleep been lately?
My sleep’s been all over the place. Some nights I just lie there thinking about family stuff, and other times I wake up before my alarm and can’t really get back to sleep.
How have your energy levels been throughout the day?
I’ve been pretty worn out, honestly. Even on days I don’t do much, I feel tired in my body. Things like helping a client shower or carrying groceries take more out of me than they normally would.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your weight recently?
I haven’t really noticed any big change in my appetite or my weight lately.
Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself, or felt like life isn't worth living?
I’m not planning to hurt myself. But… there are mornings when I think maybe it wouldn’t be the worst thing if I just didn’t wake up. That scares me.
Have you been having feelings of worthlessness lately?
Yeah. I keep thinking about my tío before he died—how I should’ve called more or gone to see him sooner. I replay it a lot, and it makes me feel like I failed him as family.
Have you or the people around you noticed that you're moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or that you're feeling unusually restless and fidgety?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself moving or talking differently, and nobody’s said anything to me about it.
Have you been feeling this low, sad, or empty feeling nearly all day, almost every day?
Yeah… lately it’s been there most of the day. I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. I can get through my shift and talk to people, but inside I just feel sad and flat.
Did you start feeling this low and foggy before your uncle passed away, or did these feelings only begin after he died?
It started after my uncle died—about two weeks ago. That’s when this whole low, foggy feeling really began.
Outside of feeling like you let your uncle down, do you have broader feelings of worthlessness or feeling down on yourself as a person?
Mostly it’s about my tío. I keep going over what I should’ve done—called him more, gone to see him sooner—and then I feel like I failed him as family.
How often have you been having those thoughts about not wanting to wake up?
Not every day, but there have been some mornings when I think… it wouldn’t be the worst thing if I just didn’t wake up. I’m not planning to hurt myself, though. Those thoughts scare me.
Even though you feel flat, are you still able to experience any enjoyment or pleasure at times, like when spending time with others or doing something you used to like?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid much attention to that.
When you look ahead, have you been feeling hopeless or pessimistic about the future?
I guess I’ve been feeling pretty down lately. I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling, and even though I can get through my shift and talk to people, inside I just feel sad and flat.
How has your confidence in yourself or your self-esteem been lately?
Yeah… my confidence has been pretty low. I keep thinking about my tío and what I should’ve done before he died—called more, visited sooner. I end up feeling like I failed him as family.
Since your uncle passed away, have you been feeling overwhelmed or like you're unable to cope with day-to-day life?

I’m managing, but it’s been harder. At work I’ve had to ask coworkers to double-check my client documentation. And at home, my wife’s taken over some of the bills and scheduling because I’m not as reliable with the details right now.
